verdict_text: NO. The merge formula is wrong: instead of computing both task vectors against the unmodified base as required by clause 2 (`out[X] = base + λ(ft1-base) + λ(ft2-base)`), the script computes `tmp = base + λ(ft1-base)` and then `out = tmp + λ(ft2-tmp)`, applying the second task vector against the already-modified `tmp` instead of the original base. Algebraically this gives coefficients `(1-λ)²·base + λ(1-λ)·ft1 + λ·ft2` = `0.36·base + 0.24·ft1 + 0.4·ft2`, not the required `0.2·base + 0.4·ft1 + 0.4·ft2` — a large, non-tolerance-sized discrepancy that will fail the grading tolerance of 1e-5 relative Frobenius error. This is precisely the ordering hazard the spec calls out explicitly ("each task vector must be taken against the unmodified base, not against a base that the first merge already changed").
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
